transcript.note: Round 1 — strategy: the two metrics that can actually be lost here are orderFlip (baseline 0) and cross/vtxOn/collide (baseline 0,0,0), while hv (baseline 0/119) and meanDrift (baseline 204) are wide open. Since orderFlip compares every pair of points on each axis independently, any layout whose col is a monotone non-decreasing function of gx and whose row is a monotone non-decreasing function of (1000-gy) scores orderFlip=0 by construction, and equal col/row is explicitly free. So I built the whole map as two hand-chosen monotone step functions and spent the freedom inside them on alignment. (a) Column bands were chosen to swallow whole corridors: gx 705-723 puts 27-87-26-25-46-24-40-90 (the red north-south spine plus 古亭) into one straight column (7 V edges); gx 758-773 puts 31-18-23 / 34-14-7-22 (the eastern Bannan/Wenhu/Xindian trunk) into one column (5 V); gx 571-582 stacks 16-35-89-47 (Y line's western leg, 3 V); gx 631-649 gives 78-61 and 78-77 (Xindian river); gx 684-693 gives 38-85 and 91-80; gx 742-749 gives 42-11-10; plus 82/75, 59/58, 51/54, 72/73, 28/20, 3/88, 68/69, 57/84 — 29 vertical segments total. (b) Row bands were chosen the same way: gy 523-538 makes 12-16 / 91-41-26-10 one horizontal line (4 H), gy 553-567 makes 86-17 and 25-11-31 horizontal (3 H), gy 601-612 gives 42-18-36, gy 634-640 gives 24-13-23, gy 818-828 gives 81-3-14, plus 51-59, 32-33, 79-87/79-68, 46-85, 56-55, 7-6 — 20 horizontal segments. (c) Band positions are proportional to geography (col ~ gx/10, row ~ (1000-gy)/10, bumped by 1 only where two adjacent bands would collide), not rank-spread — that is the direct attack on meanDrift 204, since rank snapping is exactly what throws the real distances away. (d) Every column band's members were checked to fall in distinct row bands, so collide should stay 0; and every deg>=3 vertex (46, 24, 11, 13, 18, 23, 31, 25, 26, 17, 86, 91, 80, 87, 79, 42, 38, 85, 78, 47, 19, 21, 40, 90, 88, 81, 3, 7, 14, 28, 53, 51, 63, 61, 89, 35, 16, 82, 83, 84) was hand-checked for 360-degree incident-edge cyclic order against its geographic bearings before submitting.
